**Paper:** *Copies, Conflicts and Broken Parses: How Corpus Defects Affect Retrieval-Augmented Claim Verification* — Likhith Venkata Sai Manikanta Nalla, 2026 (preprint, `paper/Nalla_2026_corpus_defects_RAG.pdf`).

New in v1.1.0 (Week 6):
- Five corruption seeds for every random defect (was two).
- Qwen2.5-3B as a second zero-shot verifier.
- Replication on Climate-FEVER (closed corpus of 5,240 evidence sentences, 1,381 claims).
- Paper in ACL format (`paper/`, LaTeX source and arXiv bundle) alongside the technical report.

Main findings: retrieval metrics rank corpus defects in the wrong order of harm (copies hurt recall@1 most but barely change verdicts; broken parsing is nearly invisible to retrieval yet costs correct answers for every verifier); stale copies with reversed findings sway a fine-tuned NLI verifier, strongly so on one-sentence Climate-FEVER records, while zero-shot LLMs largely ignore them; single-sentence chunks make the fine-tuned verifier less accurate and more confident.

Previous version: v1.0.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23314458
